lead.title: PrismML ships Ternary Bonsai 2 27B at a 5.9 GB footprint, up to 143 tok/s on an RTX 5090
lead.summary: The 27.8B multimodal model, built on Qwen3.8 27B, compresses to a 5.9 GB memory footprint, over 9x smaller than its full-precision form, and scores 83.9 on a 20-benchmark suite, 98.2% of the full-precision 85.4. PrismML reports up to 143 tokens/s on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 and 46.8 tokens/s on an M5 Max, with Apache 2.0 downloads open since September 17.

top_stories.title: llama.cpp b11040 adds ggml allocation-failure checks after a week of nightly churn
top_stories.summary: Build b11040 landed on September 18 with allocation-failure checks in ggml, alongside same-day builds b11034-b11039 that bring SWA pattern roundtripping for 15 more architectures, WebGPU get_rows fixes, Vulkan IQ3_S MMQ kernels and the ufakzeka pre-tokenizer.

top_stories.title: Anthropic stands up a Bay Area wet lab to push Claude into drug development
top_stories.summary: The new lab extends Anthropic's life-sciences work beyond computer simulation into physical biological experiments, letting Claude direct laboratory robots with limited human intervention.

top_stories.title: U.S. agencies say China's AI surge rests on industrial-scale distillation of American frontier models
top_stories.summary: The finding sharpens the debate over how to measure and rank open-weight progress, since cheaper systems are reportedly trained on outputs of U.S. frontier models.

top_stories.title: TypeSafe launches Jev, a decision-first model that skips token-by-token generation
top_stories.summary: Trained with a method the company calls RLCD, Jev produces decisions instead of streamed text, claimed at 20-200x faster inference and 40-400x lower cost.

items.title: What does privileged information add to on-policy self-distillation?
items.summary: Isolates the contribution of privileged teacher information in on-policy self-distillation for language models, quantifying how much the extra answer/worked-solution signal adds beyond the distillation mechanism itself.

items.title: QVAC Genesis III: a large open STEM corpus for small-model pre-training
items.summary: Releases an open STEM-focused pre-training corpus aimed at small language models for on-device and edge deployment under tight token budgets, evaluated against baseline SLM pre-training setups.

items.title: SoL-Pi recursively scales auto-research loops for an efficient agent harness
items.summary: Introduces a token-efficient recursive self-improvement harness for coding agents, targeting long trajectories of reasoning, tool use and feedback with improved token efficiency.

items.title: QUALS: corpus equilibrium for universal time-series forecasting
items.summary: Combines pattern quantization with learnability synchronization to train universal forecasting foundation models on heterogeneous corpora, improving zero-shot accuracy versus baselines.

items.title: Don't mask the environment: observation supervision changes agent exploration under RL
items.summary: Shows that including environment observations as prediction targets, not only agent action tokens, in SFT yields better-initialized agents for downstream RL and alters exploration behaviour.

items.title: Cactus Needle 3: 8-29 MB automation models claimed near DeepSeek V4 Flash on tool calling
items.summary: Cactus Compute's Needle 3 line covers very small on-device automation models with a claimed parity against DeepSeek V4 Flash on agentic tool-calling tasks, aimed at phones and single-board machines.

items.title: MCPJam arrives as an inspector and CI gate for MCP servers
items.summary: An open-source inspector plus CI/CD gate for Model Context Protocol servers: local playground, JSON-RPC waterfall traces, OAuth debugger and cross-client parity checks across roughly 16 AI client configurations, runnable offline via npx @mcpjam/inspector.

items.title: Forcefield: a fast, lightweight local-first agent harness in Go
items.summary: A Go agent harness built to make local models easier to drive than with Claude Code-style tooling, with simpler configuration for pointing at on-device inference.

items.title: Fouine: local full-text and semantic search for scanned PDFs on macOS
items.summary: Combines full-text and semantic search over scanned PDFs entirely on the machine, an offline RAG-style retrieval utility for macOS users running local models.

items.title: Talos: a personal agent whose kernel gates every tool call
items.summary: A personal agent framework whose kernel mediates and gates each tool call explicitly, aimed at deterministic, auditable local agent runs.

items.title: Three-line FP16 fix restores precision on Tesla P100/P40 in the TurboQuant llama.cpp fork
items.summary: The sm_61 exemption from the FP16 fast-path flag is fixed in TurboQuant v0.3.0, so the ~80 USD P100 (16 GB HBM2, 732 GB/s) again accumulates in FP32 with cleaner outputs, narrowing the old gap against the P40 on budget homelab rigs.

items.title: n8n Gateway credits pool model providers behind one prepaid balance
items.summary: From n8n v2.36, Cloud plans can reach six model providers and five tool services through a shared prepaid Gateway credit balance instead of per-provider accounts and keys, with per-workflow usage in the admin panel; self-host support is still pending.

items.title: n8n source-control push CVE patched in 1.123.76, 2.37.7 and 2.38.2
items.summary: CVE-2026-92588 (medium, 5.9) covers cross-project data destruction via the source control push endpoint, which trusted client-supplied file paths; operators with Environments enabled should upgrade.

items.title: n8n 2.39.7 fixes breaking-change detection and numeric credential inputs
items.summary: The stable patch keeps breaking-change detection running when a rule throws (#38790) and sends number values correctly in credential inputs (#38881); the 1.x LTS line separately got 1.123.81 with credential-scope handling plus undici 7.29.1, vm2 3.12.2 and Snowflake SDK 3.3.0 bumps for pinned deployments.

items.title: Home Assistant 2026.9.3 patch lands September 18
items.summary: The patch follows 2026.9.1 (Sep 5) and 2026.9.2 (Sep 11) on top of a September core release that consolidated Modbus device connections under a single shared connection.

items.title: TensorRT Edge-LLM posts an MLPerf Edge Agentic result on Jetson AGX Thor
items.summary: On the MLPerf Inference v6.1 Edge Agentic benchmark, Qwen3.6-27B on a single Jetson AGX Thor Developer Kit (128 GB unified memory, MAXN power mode) hit 52.33 tokens/s output and completed 1,007 workload turns in 24 minutes 36 seconds, leaning on NVFP4 weights/activations, an FP8 KV cache and a 16-node speculative decoding tree worth roughly 40% more decoding speed than linear MTP.

items.title: Apple plans M8 Ultra AI servers; Huawei shows off Atlas 960 SuperPoD
items.summary: Apple is developing dedicated AI servers around future M8 Ultra processors in two- and four-chip configurations for developers, enterprises and governments with no arrival before 2029, and is studying Nvidia NVLink Fusion; Huawei's Atlas 960 SuperPoD and Peerium architecture link up to a million processors as one computer via nested parallelism, unified memory addressing and peer interconnect.

items.title: Memory wall dominates the hardware brief: server memory spend headed for $175-190B by 2027
items.summary: A typical AI server uses roughly eight times more memory than a traditional one, and AI server memory spend is projected to jump from $35 billion in 2025 to $175-190 billion by 2027, with Qualcomm moving from HBM to a proprietary high-bandwidth layout and d-Matrix's Raptor chip on higher-throughput 3D DRAM as competing answers.

items.title: RPCS3 workaround for an NVIDIA driver bug lifts GeForce performance 20-25%
items.summary: Measured gains of 20% on an RTX 3080 and 25% on an RTX 5090 follow the PS3 emulator's fix for a driver bug that had suppressed performance across most PlayStation 3 titles on GeForce hardware.

items.title: Leak: RTX 60 series slips to 2028, AMD may ship one RDNA 5 chip next year
items.summary: An AnandTech-affiliated leak claims Nvidia's RTX 60-series holds until 2028 while AMD launches only the mid-range AT2 in 2027; neither company has confirmed, and memory-driven prices are expected to stay high.
